previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with chronic pancreatitis, seizure disorder, diabetes, and bipolar disorder was admitted after experiencing a seizure en route to the hospital for worsening abdominal pain, nausea, and vomiting. He had recently undergone stent placement and reported no improvement. Labs showed leukocytosis, low antiepileptic drug levels, and metabolic acidosis, which resolved with IV fluids. CT confirmed acute on chronic pancreatitis with peripancreatic stranding. The pancreatic stent was removed via ERCP due to persistent symptoms. His pain improved, he was advanced to a full diet, and his seizure medications were adjusted. A rash and enlarged lymph node behind the ear were noted; he was treated with topical steroids and a course of dicloxacillin for possible cellulitis. He was discharged home in good condition, tolerating oral intake, with instructions to follow up on his pancreas condition, lymph node, and medications.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ man with right upper quadrant pain.

Comparison is made to the prior CT of the abdomen performed on ___.

FINDINGS:  The gallbladder contains multiple stones.  No gallbladder wall
thickening or wall edema is noted. No sonographic ___ sign was
appreciated. No ascites is noted.  An 8 mm echogenic round lesion is seen
within the upper pole of the right kidney without posterior acoustic
shadowing, likely representing a small angiomyolipoma. The common bile duct is
normal in size measuring 3 mm. Imaged portion of the liver is unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Cholelithiasis without evidence of acute cholecystitis.

2.  Probable small angiomyolipoma of upper pole of the right kidney.

INDICATION:  Upper abdominal pain.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph, ___.

UPRIGHT AP VIEW OF THE CHEST:  Cardiac, mediastinal, and hilar contours are
within normal limits and unchanged.  The pulmonary vascularity is normal.  The
lungs are clear.  No focal consolidation, pleural effusion, or pneumothorax is
identified.  No free air is seen under the diaphragms.  Osseous structures are
unchanged.

IMPRESSION:  No acute cardiopulmonary abnormality.

Additional comments: Multiple calcifications are seen within an atrophic
pancreas compatible with chronic pancreas (the report above states multiple
stones, which is incorrect). No features of acute pancreatitis are evident.
Additionally, several subcutaneous nodules are noted within the anterior
abdominal wall, compatible with sites of subcutaneous injections (the patient
admininsters insulin).  Additionally, a small fat containing umbilical hernia
is present.

INDICATION:  ___ man with right upper quadrant pain and right flank
pain.

Comparison is made to the same day ultrasound.

TECHNIQUE:  Axial MDCT images of the abdomen were obtained after
administration of 100 cc of Optiray intravenously.  Sagittal and coronal
reformatted images were then obtained.

CT of the abdomen with contrast: The visualized portion of the lung bases does
not demonstrate any pulmonary nodule or pleural effusion or parenchymal
consolidation.

The liver, spleen, adrenal glands, and kidneys have normal appearance.
Cholelithiasis with no evidence of cholecystitis.  Multiple stones are noted
within the atrophic pancreas which has a mildly distended duct and are
compatible with reported history of chronic pancreatitis.  There has been
interval removal of the pancreatic stent.  The stomach, duodenum, loops of
small bowel and large bowel and appendix have normal appearance.  No
pathologically enlarged lymph nodes are noted within retroperitoneum or
mesentery.  No free fluid or air is noted within the abdomen or pelvis.

CT OF THE PELVIS WITH CONTRAST:  The urinary bladder, distal ureters, rectum,
sigmoid colon and the prostate gland have normal appearance.

BONE WINDOWS:  No concerning lytic or sclerotic lesions are identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Cholelithiasis with no evidence of cholecystitis.

2.  Unchnaged chronic pancreatitis.

3.  Interval removal of the pancreatic stent.
